purpose: Durable chef-facing cover-production contract for Vikings 2026. It separates issue-specific cover composition from series-wide trade-dress authority and requires actual pixel inspection of the released Issue 1 cover before later-cover generation.

authority.issueRecipe: The exact assembled VIK_S1E##_COVER RexPrompt recipe controls the issue-specific selling image, cast, environment, composition, spoiler ceiling, and exact issue lettering.
authority.tradeDress: The released Vikings 2026 Issue 1 cover in StarSplitterVisions controls masthead architecture, publisher badge, VIKINGS 2026! wordmark treatment, year/issue box, horizontal-rule language, issue-strapline placement, top-band proportions, and restrained dark-on-white publication design.
authority.characterWorld: Released StarSplitterVisions pages plus approved current-production references control established character identity, costumes, locations, props, rendering language, and later story state.
authority.scopeRule: Trade-dress authority does not authorize copying the Issue 1 scene composition into later covers. Later cover images are controlled by their own assembled cover recipes.

canonicalTradeDressReference.requiredUse: pixel-read before every Vikings cover generation
canonicalTradeDressReference.pixelReadRule: Retrieve and inspect the actual local reference pixels in active multimodal context. Repository path, SHA, metadata, prose description, memory, or a statement that the image was previously viewed is not a substitute for current pixel inspection.

observedTradeDress.mastheadField: Large white horizontal field occupying the upper portion of the portrait cover, visually separated from the illustration by dark horizontal rules.
observedTradeDress.publisherBadge: Boxed Star Splitter / VISIONS mark at upper left with star device; year and issue number are contained in the lower portion of the same vertical badge.
observedTradeDress.seriesWordmark: Huge dark condensed all-caps VIKINGS 2026! wordmark spanning the masthead to the right of the publisher badge.
observedTradeDress.issueStrapline: Narrow all-caps line beneath the wordmark, bracketed by thin horizontal rules. For later issues this line carries the issue title.
observedTradeDress.colorLogic: Restrained dark navy/black typography and rules on white masthead; the illustration carries the issue-specific color.
observedTradeDress.letteringRule: Keep the publication architecture stable while changing only issue number and issue strapline. Do not add blurbs, slogans, price bursts, fake barcodes, variant labels, creator credits, or other unscripted promotional copy.
observedTradeDress.compositionRule: The cover illustration begins beneath the masthead. Later issue art should vary boldly by issue while preserving the masthead proportions and overall publication identity.
observedTradeDress.designIntent: Deliberately bland municipal-publication shell. The masthead should read like an earnest City of New York agency bulletin or public-information document that has accidentally become the cover of an extraordinary comic. The bureaucratic top band must not compete with the illustration; its visual dullness is part of the series identity.
observedTradeDress.commercialContrast: The trade dress supplies deadpan institutional normalcy; the painted image beneath it supplies desire, drama, human specificity and commercial appeal. Do not make the masthead cooler to make the cover more sellable.

coverRecipeSource.rule: Use the assembled cover recipe, not raw metadata alone. The chef must receive the exact assembled recipe and then resolve pixel references before generation.

mandatoryReferenceGate: Resolve the requested Vikings cover show and assemble the exact VIK_S1E##_COVER recipe.

Retrieve and visually inspect the actual pixels of production/references/vikings-2026/assets/covers/issue-01-cover-trade-dress.jpg. This local asset is an exact byte-for-byte copy of the released StarSplitterVisions Issue 1 cover.
Use those pixels only for trade dress, masthead, publication typography architecture, border/rule language, and cover-brand continuity.
Resolve actual released or approved pixels for every recurring character or established location materially present on the cover.
Use the current cover recipe for the issue-specific hook, cast, composition, environment, spoiler ceiling, and exact issue text.
Confirm the proposed illustration is one dominant selling image and remains legible at thumbnail size.
Generate only after all applicable visual references are present as pixels in active multimodal context.
coverQualityGate: One-second read: the dominant issue hook is legible immediately.
Thumbnail test: focal silhouette, major shape system, and masthead remain clear when reduced.

Municipal masthead test: the upper band reads as a boring official public-agency publication, not a flashy comic logo treatment; no Norse/fantasy/commercial embellishment has leaked into the trade dress.

New York indifference test: on public covers, surrounding New Yorkers continue ordinary tasks without gawking, pointing, photographing or turning the displaced Norse characters into a spectacle; on private covers, do not invent spectators merely to satisfy this rule.
Series test: masthead/trade dress unmistakably belongs to Vikings 2026.
Issue test: the image could not be casually reassigned to a different issue.
Spoiler test: cover promises pressure without revealing the issue's solution, reversal, ruling, or final payoff.
Tone test: grounded documentary-comedy dignity; humor comes from incompatible systems and ordinary New York indifference rather than caricature.
Composition test: no recap collage, floating-head montage, generic cast lineup, or fake action spectacle unless an exact cover recipe explicitly requires it.
Lettering test: exact series wordmark, year/issue number, and issue strapline only; no invented promotional text.
Reference test: recurring characters and world elements match actual established pixels rather than prose reconstruction.

issueLettering.strapline: AT THE MUNICIPAL TEMPORAL DISPLACEMENT INTEGRATION DEPARTMENT

coverLineDoctrine: Every cover sells one dominant issue-specific contradiction or desire rather than summarizing the issue.
The masthead remains deliberately municipal, official, rigid and visually boring; the image beneath it is the sales engine.
The Norse characters remain visibly ninth-century and therefore materially out of place inside modern New York. Do not solve the contrast by visually modernizing them.

When a cover occurs in public, ordinary New Yorkers generally continue their own tasks rather than stopping to stare. Background indifference is a recurring New York worldbuilding language, not a one-off gag.
The public should not point, laugh, photograph, surround, recoil from, or perform astonishment at the Vikings unless a specific story beat explicitly requires such behavior.
New York indifference remains subordinate to the issue hook: use a few legible routine behaviors, not a crowd-comedy tableau.
Private-space covers may express the same theme through the city or institution continuing without needing the Vikings rather than by inventing bystanders.
Covers must remain spoiler-safe, issue-specific and legible at thumbnail size.
